correctness.rationale: For \(t\le2\), the focal paper gives \(C_t^B(X)\le C_2^B(X)\le C_2(X)=C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X)\). Clarkson's exact value on real \(\ell_p\) and \(L_p\) is \(2^{|2/p-1|}\). For \(p\le2\), disjoint normalized vectors/functions are exactly Birkhoff orthogonal and have equal endpoint chords of length \(2^{1/p}\). For \(p\ge2\), the balanced two-coordinate/two-half pair is Birkhoff orthogonal and has equal endpoint chords of length \(2^{1-1/p}\). The endpoint cases \(p=1\) and \(p=\infty\) are checked directly. Thus the lower bound equals the unrestricted upper bound in every quantified case. No experiment or partial enumeration is used.

originality.rationale: The focal paper defines the Birkhoff-restricted Takahashi scale and proves the upper comparison with the unrestricted constant, but its classical \(\ell_p^2\) section gives only a balanced-family lower bound and the asymptotic limit as \(p\to\infty\), not the exact finite-\(p\) formula or the \(L_p[0,1]\) case. The closest later exact theorem is for direct isosceles orthogonality, a different admissibility relation. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches for the Birkhoff invariant, exact formula, power-mean range, and equivalent aliases found no covering statement; the available current and prior research records contain no same claim.
residual_risks: The proof is short and uses classical extremal pairs, so an equivalent Birkhoff-restricted exactness observation could exist implicitly under terminology not indexed by the targeted searches.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete benchmark for a newly introduced geometric invariant: it determines the exact constant simultaneously for all classical real sequence \(\ell_p\) spaces of dimension at least two, for real \(L_p[0,1]\), and for the full structurally distinguished range \(t\le2\). It upgrades the focal paper's one-family lower bound and asymptotic statement to a closed formula, identifies the Hilbert threshold and both Hanner/Clarkson branches, and shows that the Birkhoff restriction is exactly nonbinding in this regime. The parameter range is not an arbitrary slice: \(t=2\) is where the source's power-mean scale meets the classical von Neumann–Jordan constant and monotonicity controls every lower order.
